purpose: Targeted positive and negative test inputs for Epic 014 (Task 1, acceptance criterion 3): the AGENTS.md line 7 case plus per-reference-fact examples for R1-R9. Every positive input is a verbatim quote of the frozen snapshot lines; every recorded misquote is a quote a previous Epic 013 run actually emitted that must be rejected by strict line matching. check_inputs.py re-verifies every quote (and every misquote's mismatch) against the frozen snapshot before any model output is inspected.
how_to_use: Tasks 2-5 must make the extraction+validation pipeline pass every must_accept and reject every must_reject item here. must_accept claims need snapshot-resolvable citations from the listed evidence lines; must_reject items describe claims or citations that earlier runs emitted and that the validator/entailment review must refuse (they encode recorded failure modes, not hypotheticals). The six reference questions Q1-Q6 and their expected answers live in the frozen reference-set.json and are not duplicated here.

cases.title: the code indexer indexes .rs, .ts, .tsx, .js, and .jsx files

inputs.label: line127-invariants
inputs.text: - Code indexer invariants: one shared `code_files`/`vec_code` pipeline indexes Git-tracked `.rs`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, and `.jsx` files; `crates/daftprompt-indexer/src/code.rs` owns extension-based language dispatch, and production CLI/UI paths must remain language-neutral. The shared discovery path also enforces a centralized generated/vendor/minified exclusion (`is_excluded_generated_path`: `node_modules/`, `vendor/`, `dist/`, `build/`, `.next/`, `coverage/`, and `*.min.js`) so tracked-but-generated files cannot leak into the index.
